evidence.observation: The proposal motivates PlanReview as evidence required before implementation begins without qualifying the self-hosting migration path.
The task plan explicitly migrates the change after the implementation tasks are already completed, making this generation's review retrospective for those tasks.
The migration plan obtains PlanReview only during the late self-migration step after implementation of the new machinery.

findings.summary: Explain why retrospective review is acceptable for this named bootstrap and state exactly which assurance it does and does not provide. The current WHY presents a prospective-before-implementation benefit that this self-hosting generation cannot realize.

evidence.observation: The proposal also places exact-diff AI review outside the current change.
The only remaining adoption task says exact-diff AI review remains assigned to T2.3 and does not define a separate exact-diff review deliverable or acceptance evidence.
Migration step 9 requires an independent exact-diff review of the trust core.

findings.summary: Resolve whether migration step 9 requires a current-change exact-diff review. If it means a non-AI review, define its reviewer, subject, evidence, and pass criteria; otherwise remove it from this generation through replanning.

evidence.observation: The claim registry assigns C-AVAILABILITY to a T1.5 empirical pilot covering wait, grant, latency, and cost budgets.

Task 7.1 conditionally requests a 'healthy' Codex/Claude pilot when both adapters are available but defines neither health criteria nor durable evidence for unavailable, partial, latency, or cost outcomes.

findings.summary: Make the pilot testable: specify measured budgets, required observations, retained evidence, and the accepted outcome when one or both providers are unavailable. Otherwise C-AVAILABILITY cannot be evaluated consistently.

evidence.observation: The post-execution revision scenario only requires no active session and invalidation of dependent evidence; it does not define how completed task projections, generated handoff state, or task status are reconciled when the task contract changes.

Task 6.7 requires preserving completed checkbox projections during migration, but supplies no acceptance criteria for distinguishing still-valid completed work from work invalidated by the revised contract.

findings.summary: Define and test every consumer of post-execution planning revision state: completed checkbox projections, semantic task history, generated handoff/status, and eligibility of later lifecycle transitions. Evidence invalidation alone leaves completed-task behavior ambiguous.

submission.residualRisk: Even after these challenges are resolved, semantic search completeness, WHY truth, provider identity, same-user containment, and reviewer judgment remain explicitly soft or residual claims. The review also cannot establish whether completed implementation conforms to the revised plan; that requires separately bound implementation evidence.
submission.uncertainty: The immutable target does not include the eventual plan-review.json projection because this invocation is producing that review. The review therefore assesses the bound proposal, design, specifications, execution policy, guard, investigation projection, and tasks, but not the later materialized review artifact or runtime pilot records.
